questions.question_text: What market price point is established where buyer demand exactly matches seller supply?
What happens to the market price of a commodity when supply is high but buyer demand is very low?
Explain how buyer negotiation and seller bargaining lead to a agreed market price.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Sellers start with an asking price; buyers counter-offer based on perceived value. Through bargaining, they meet at a mutually acceptable price where the transaction occurs.

questions.question_text: How do Demand and Supply interact to influence commodity prices?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: High demand + Low supply = Price increases (shortage). Low demand + High supply = Price decreases (surplus). Equal demand and supply = Stable equilibrium price.

questions.question_text: Detail the core components that constitute a functional economic market in modern society.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Buyers and Sellers: Individuals or firms seeking to purchase or sell goods/services. 2) Commodities & Services: Items being traded with defined quality standards. 3) Price Discovery Mechanism: Interaction of supply and demand establishing prices. 4) Communication & Payment Channels: Physical meetings or electronic apps enabling transactions.

questions.question_text: Case Study: In a weekly fruit market, guava sellers start selling at ₹80/kg. By evening, with many guava crates unsold, sellers drop the price to ₹40/kg, causing buyers to buy all remaining stock. Identify the economic setting, define equilibrium price, and explain how supply surplus forced the price drop.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Economic Setting: Physical Retail Market. Equilibrium Price: The price (₹40/kg) where the quantity sellers wish to sell equals the quantity buyers wish to purchase. Supply Surplus Mechanism: Excess unsold guavas threatened loss through spoilage; sellers lowered prices to boost buyer demand and clear inventory.

questions.question_text: Which western Indian city is world-famous as a major historical and modern textile and diamond manufacturing hub?
Who in the supply chain purchases goods in large bulk quantities directly from textile factories?
What intermediate market actor links regional wholesalers to small neighborhood Kirana shops?
Trace the sequence of the physical supply chain for cotton garments from farm to consumer.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Cotton Farmer -> Spinning Mill -> Weaving Factory -> Wholesaler / Warehouses -> Regional Distributor -> Neighborhood Retailer -> Final Consumer.

questions.question_text: What vital economic role do wholesalers play in the distribution supply chain?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Wholesalers buy massive bulk stocks from producers, absorb storage risks in warehouses, and break bulk quantities into smaller lots for regional retailers.

questions.question_text: Examine the complete supply chain ecosystem of the Surat textile industry from raw material sourcing to global exports.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Raw Material Sourcing: Farmers supply raw cotton to ginning and spinning mills. 2) Industrial Manufacturing: Surat weaving and dyeing factories produce finished cloth rolls. 3) Wholesale Mandis: Massive wholesale markets (like Surat Textile Market) stock goods in godowns. 4) Distribution & Retail: Distributors transport cloth nationwide to retail shops and global export markets.

questions.question_text: Case Study: A cotton saree produced in a Surat factory passes through a textile wholesaler, a regional garment distributor in Patna, and a neighborhood retail saree shop before being bought by a customer. Identify the manufacturing hub, list all supply chain links in order, and explain the function of the retail shop.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Manufacturing Hub: Surat (Gujarat). Supply Chain Links: Cotton Farmer -> Surat Weaving Factory -> Textile Wholesaler -> Regional Distributor (Patna) -> Neighborhood Saree Retailer -> Final Consumer. Function of Retailer: Provides convenient local shopping access, displays small varied stocks, offers personal customer assistance, and sells single items directly to consumers.

questions.question_text: What type of traditional market sets up on a specific day of the week in temporary street stalls?
What type of modern market platform aggregates products from multiple sellers on smartphone apps for doorstep delivery?
What market deals in bulk agricultural grain sales directly between farmers and large trade buyers?
options: B) Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC / Wholesale Mandi)
questions.correct_answer: B) Agricultural Produce Market Committee (APMC / Wholesale Mandi)

questions.question_text: Compare Weekly Haats (traditional markets) with modern Shopping Malls across goods, prices, and buyers.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Weekly Haats: Offer cheap everyday groceries/clothes in open street stalls through bargaining for low-income buyers. Malls: Offer branded luxury goods in air-conditioned shops at fixed high prices for urban buyers.

questions.question_text: How do e-commerce aggregators connect buyers and sellers online?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Aggregator apps host digital catalogs of multiple sellers. Buyers browse, order, and pay online, while aggregator logistics fleets deliver items directly to homes.

questions.question_text: Analyze the advantages and disadvantages of traditional physical neighborhood retail markets versus online e-commerce platforms.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Neighborhood Retail: Advantages = Immediate product inspection, personal relationship/credit, zero waiting time; Disadvantages = Limited stock variety and fixed local hours. 2) Online E-commerce: Advantages = 24/7 shopping, vast global product selection, doorstep delivery, easy price comparison; Disadvantages = Delivery wait times, inability to physically inspect goods before purchase, digital payment barrier.

questions.question_text: Case Study: Consumer A buys fresh vegetables at a Thursday weekly haat after bargaining. Consumer B buys a branded smartphone from an online e-commerce aggregator app with home delivery. Consumer C buys 100 sacks of wheat at an APMC wholesale mandi. Identify the market typology used by Consumers A, B, and C, and detail two advantages of online aggregators.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Consumer A Market: Traditional Weekly Market (Haat). Consumer B Market: Online E-Commerce Aggregator Platform. Consumer C Market: Wholesale Agricultural Mandi (APMC). Advantages of Online Aggregators: 1) Allows 24/7 shopping convenience with direct home delivery. 2) Provides access to vast product ranges and price comparison across thousands of sellers.

questions.question_text: What price ceiling limit printed on packaged goods represents the maximum price a retailer can legally charge?
What price floor is announced by the government to guarantee farmers a minimum income for their crops?
Why does the government impose price ceilings on essential life-saving medicines?
options: B) To make essential healthcare affordable and prevent vendor price-gouging
questions.correct_answer: B) To make essential healthcare affordable and prevent vendor price-gouging

questions.question_text: What is Maximum Retail Price (MRP), and why is charging above MRP illegal?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: MRP is the maximum legal price printed on packaged goods including all taxes. Charging above MRP exploits consumers and violates consumer protection laws.

questions.question_text: How does Minimum Support Price (MSP) protect farmers during bumper harvest gluts?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: When crop oversupply crashes open market prices, the government purchases farm crops directly at the pre-announced MSP floor, preventing farmer distress sales.

questions.question_text: Evaluate government interventions in economic markets through floor prices (MSP), ceiling prices (MRP), and public distribution systems.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Floor Prices (MSP): Protect farm producers from price crashes during crop gluts, securing rural livelihoods. 2) Ceiling Prices (MRP & Fair Price Shops): Protect consumers from artificial hoarding, monopoly price-gouging, and inflation on food/medicine. 3) Regulatory Balance: Ensures markets remain fair, transparent, and socially equitable for both poor buyers and vulnerable producers.

questions.question_text: Case Study: A shopkeeper tries to charge ₹60 for a milk packet with a printed MRP of ₹50. Meanwhile, wheat farmers sell grain to government procurement centers at an MSP of ₹2,125 per quintal when open markets crash to ₹1,500. Identify the two government price mechanisms (MRP and MSP), explain the legal status of charging above MRP, and state how MSP saves farmers.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Price Mechanisms: MRP = Maximum Retail Price (Price Ceiling); MSP = Minimum Support Price (Price Floor). Legal Status of MRP: Charging above MRP is a punishable legal offense under consumer protection laws. How MSP Saves Farmers: Acts as a guaranteed financial safety net; government buys crops at MSP so farmers do not suffer bankruptcy when private traders offer crash prices.

questions.question_text: Which government certification mark guarantees safety and quality standards for industrial manufactured products in India?
Which regulatory authority certifies food safety standards and hygiene for packaged food products in India?
Which certification label on electrical appliances indicates energy efficiency and electricity savings?
List four mandatory items of information that must be printed on packaged food labels.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1. Net weight/quantity. 2. Maximum Retail Price (MRP). 3. Manufacturing and Expiry/Best Before date. 4. FSSAI License Number and Ingredients list.

questions.question_text: What quality assurance do AGMARK and BIS Hallmark logos provide to consumers?
questions.marking_scheme_answer: AGMARK certifies the quality and purity of agricultural food products (oil, honey, ghee); BIS Hallmark certifies the purity of gold and silver jewelry.

questions.question_text: Examine consumer rights and the importance of quality certification logos in protecting citizens against adulteration and unsafe products.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: 1) Protection against Adulteration: FSSAI and AGMARK ensure food products are free from harmful chemicals or fake ingredients. 2) Product Safety: ISI mark guarantees electrical appliances will not cause fires or shocks. 3) Energy Efficiency: BEE Star ratings help consumers choose energy-saving appliances that reduce power bills. 4) Consumer Empowerment: Mandatory packaging labels allow informed choices and legal redress.

questions.question_text: Case Study: A consumer buys a 1 kg packet of ghee displaying an AGMARK logo, an FSSAI license number, and a manufacturing date of Jan 2026 with 'Best Before 12 Months'. They also buy a 5-star BEE rated refrigerator bearing an ISI mark. Identify the quality logos for agricultural purity (AGMARK), food safety (FSSAI), electrical safety (ISI), and energy savings (BEE Star), and explain why checking packaging labels protects consumer health and finance.
questions.marking_scheme_answer: Quality Logos Identified: AGMARK = Agricultural food purity; FSSAI = Food safety & hygiene license; ISI = Industrial electrical safety compliance; BEE Star = Energy efficiency rating. Packaging Label Protection: 1) Health Protection: Verifying expiry dates and FSSAI numbers prevents consuming spoiled or chemical-adulterated food. 2) Financial Protection: Checking MRP prevents overcharging, while BEE star ratings lower monthly electricity bills.
